newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina says no immediate plan for Sigma unit.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina says no immediate plan for Sigma unit.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Belgian oil group PetroFina said on Tuesday the company had no immediate plans for its Sigma paints division.
"It's not the time to spin off an activity which needs the support of the group to return to full profitability," spokeswoman Catherine Ferrant told Reuters.
Ferrant was asked to comment on a newspaper interview in which PetroFina chief executive officer Francois Cornelis seemed to imply Sigma could be separated from the rest of the group.

"I must admit that Sigma's activities do not really fit in with PetroFina's other businesses. The ideal scenario would be to make Sigma strong enough so that the company can realise its potential as an independent company," Cornelis told the Tuesday edition of Belgian daily De Standaard.
Ferrant said, however, this did not mean that PetroFina was planning to sell the company or separate it from its core petroleum and petrochemical businesses in the near term.

Ferrant confirmed that PetroFina sees group profit, before deduction of minority interests, of around 15 billion Belgian francs in 1996, up from 12.3 billion in 1995. PetroFina had a 1995 group net profit, less minorities, of 11.6 billion francs.
She also confirmed the company was looking to expand its retail petrol station network into Poland and Spain.
